text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman has won a sweeping victory in presidential elections securing his second mandate, first preliminary results show.
- A very low turnout at polls in Eastern Slavonia. Only 1,138 of the total 10,925 registered voters in Vukovar cast their ballots by 0400 p.m on Sunday.
- Croatia is facing a difficult political and diplomatic battle for war damages from Serbia and Montenegro, says expert Mate Pavkovic.
- Money market: Stonger kuna supply brought lending rates down last week.
- Better legal regulation of the short-term securities is vital, says head of Zagreb's money market Josip Gotovac.
- Nikolina Slavujevic of Zagrebacka Banka elected presidnet of the brokers' association.
- Vlado Gotovac and Zdravko Tomac, contenders in the presidential race, say they are disappointed with turnout.
- Bosnian Croats, who were entitled to vote in Sunday's Croatian presidential elections, flocked to the polling stations in unprecedented numbers causing havoc.
- The European Bank plans to financing up to 30 percent of a new thermoelectric plant on the Adriatic coast, says Damir Begovic, head of the state electricity board HEP.

- Romanian illegal immigrants pay between 500 and 1,000 German marks to cross Croatia's southern border with Montenegro on their way to Western Europe. On average, crossings take place twice a month in groups of four to eight people.
- Croatian tourist workers had to stop Italian sales of holiday packages on the coast in August because of overbookings. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
